steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your eyes directly under the bar, which should be resting on the metal hooks above you. Put both feet flat on the floor.
Reach up and grab the bar with both hands, a little wider than your shoulders. Wrap your thumbs all the way around the bar so it can't slip out.
Pull your shoulder blades together and press them down into the bench, like you're tucking them into your back pockets. Keep them there for the whole set.
Lift the bar off the hooks and hold it straight above your chest with your arms straight.
Slowly lower the bar to the middle of your chest. Let your elbows angle out about halfway, not straight out to the sides.
Let the bar lightly touch your chest, then push it back up in a straight line until your arms are straight again.
watchFor: Never bounce the bar off your chest, and keep your hips and head on the bench the whole time.
If you're new, start with just the empty bar and add weight a little at a time. Set the rack's safety bars just below your chest, or have someone stand behind the bench in case you get stuck.
Keep your wrists straight, stacked over your forearms, not bent backward.

steps: Set the bench so the back is tilted upward at a slight angle, about 30 degrees. Lie back on it with your eyes directly under the bar and both feet flat on the floor.
Grab the bar with both hands, slightly wider than your shoulders, with your thumbs wrapped around it.
Pull your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench. Keep them there for the whole set.
Lift the bar off the hooks and hold it straight above your upper chest with your arms straight.
Lower the bar slowly to the top of your chest, just below your collarbone, with your elbows angled out about halfway.
Touch the bar lightly to your chest, then push it straight back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't set the bench too steep. Past about 45 degrees the work shifts to your shoulders and puts more strain on them.
Don't bounce the bar off your chest or arch your lower back off the bench.
Start light and use the rack's safety bars, or have someone stand behind you, so a missed lift is never a problem.

steps: Lie back on a bench that slopes downward, with your head lower than your hips. Hook your legs securely under the padded rollers at the end.
Reach up and grab the bar with both hands, a little wider than your shoulders, thumbs wrapped around it.
Pull your shoulder blades together and press them into the bench.
Lift the bar off the hooks and hold it straight above your lower chest with your arms straight.
Slowly lower the bar to the lower part of your chest, keeping your elbows angled out about halfway.
Touch the bar lightly to your chest, then press it straight back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Get on and off the bench slowly. Lying with your head lower than your body can make you dizzy if you stand up too fast.
This position makes it harder to put the bar back if you get stuck, so start light and have someone stand behind you to help.
Never bounce the bar off your chest.

steps: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell standing on each thigh. Lie back and use your legs to help swing the dumbbells up to chest height, one at a time.
Put both feet flat on the floor and pull your shoulder blades together against the bench.
Hold the dumbbells above your chest with your arms straight and your palms facing your feet.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to either side of your chest. Your elbows should angle out about halfway, and your forearms should stay straight up and down.
When you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, push the dumbbells back up until your arms are straight and the weights are almost touching.
watchFor: Pick a weight you can control. When you're finished, don't drop the weights: rest them back on your thighs and sit up, or lower them gently to the floor beside you.
Don't let your elbows drop far below the bench. Stop when the dumbbells are level with your chest.
Keep your wrists straight, not bent backward.

steps: Set the bench back so it slopes upward at a slight angle, about 30 degrees. Sit down with a dumbbell standing on each thigh.
Lie back and swing the dumbbells up to your chest one at a time, using your legs to help. Put both feet flat on the floor.
Pull your shoulder blades together against the bench.
Push the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your upper chest, with your palms facing forward.
Slowly lower them to either side of your upper chest, with your elbows angled out about halfway.
Press them back up until your arms are straight and the weights are almost touching.
watchFor: Keep the bench angle gentle. If it's too steep, your shoulders take over and get strained.
Choose a weight you can control the whole way down. Setting the dumbbells down safely at the end matters: rest them on your thighs before you sit up.
Don't let your back arch off the bench.

steps: Lie back on a bench that slopes downward with your head lower than your hips. Hook your legs under the padded rollers at the end so you can't slide.
Have a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs as you lie back, then bring them up to chest height.
Hold them above your lower chest with your arms straight and your palms facing your feet.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to either side of your lower chest, with your elbows angled out about halfway.
Push them back up until your arms are straight and the weights are almost touching.
watchFor: Lying with your head lower than your body can make you dizzy. Get up slowly when you're done.
Getting heavy dumbbells into position on this bench is awkward, so start light and don't rush the setup.
Don't let your elbows drop far below the bench.

steps: Lie on your back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Put both feet flat on the floor.
Hold the dumbbells straight above your chest with your palms facing each other and a small, soft bend in your elbows.
Keeping that bend in your elbows the whole time, slowly open your arms out to your sides in a wide arc, like you're opening a big hug.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest. Stop when your hands are about level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc until they're almost touching above you.
watchFor: Use light weights. This move puts your shoulders in a stretched position, so heavy weights can strain them.
Don't lower your arms past the level of your chest, and don't straighten or bend your elbows more during the move. Keep the same slight bend throughout.

steps: Set the bench so it slopes upward at a slight angle, about 30 degrees. Lie back on it with a dumbbell in each hand and both feet flat on the floor.
Hold the dumbbells above your upper chest with your palms facing each other and a small, soft bend in your elbows.
Keeping that bend in your elbows, slowly open your arms out to your sides in a wide arc, like opening a big hug.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, with your hands about level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your chest and bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc until they almost touch.
watchFor: Use light weights. The stretched position at the bottom can strain your shoulders if the weight is too heavy.
Keep the bench angle gentle, and keep the same bend in your elbows the whole time.

steps: Set both cable pulleys to the highest position and attach a handle to each one.
Stand in the middle, one foot slightly in front of the other for balance. Take a handle in each hand and step forward so the cables pull your arms out and back.
Lean forward slightly from your hips, keep your back flat, and keep a small bend in your elbows.
Pull the handles down and together in a wide arc until your hands meet in front of your lower chest.
Squeeze your chest for a moment, then slowly let your arms open back up until you feel a stretch across your chest.
watchFor: Keep the bend in your elbows the same throughout. Don't turn it into a pushing or pulling motion.
Pick a weight you can control on the way back out. If the cables yank your arms back, it's too heavy.

steps: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position and attach a handle to each one.
Stand between them, one foot slightly in front of the other. Take a handle in each hand with your palms facing up and forward.
Keep a small bend in your elbows and your chest lifted.
Sweep your hands up and together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your face, about at eye level.
Squeeze your upper chest, then slowly lower your arms back down and out along the same path.
watchFor: Keep your elbows softly bent the whole time, and don't shrug your shoulders up toward your ears.
Choose a weight you can control on the way down.

steps: Set both cable pulleys to the highest position and attach a handle to each one.
Stand between them, one foot slightly in front of the other, and take a handle in each hand.
Lean forward a little from your hips with your back flat, and keep a small bend in your elbows.
Sweep your hands down and together in a wide arc until they meet in front of your lower stomach or hips.
Squeeze your lower chest, then slowly let your arms rise back up along the same path.
watchFor: Keep the bend in your elbows the same throughout, and don't hunch your shoulders.
If your back rounds or you have to swing your body to move the weight, lower the weight.

steps: Sit down and adjust the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest. Set the weight before you sit if you can.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Take hold of the handles with your palms facing down or forward, whichever the machine is built for.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight. Don't force your elbows all the way back.
Slowly let the handles come back until you feel a stretch across your chest, then push again.
watchFor: Keep your shoulders down and back against the pad. Don't let them roll forward as you push.
Don't slam the weight stack on the way back. Control the handles the whole way.

steps: Sit on the seat and adjust it so the handles or arm pads are level with your chest.
Keep your back flat against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Place your forearms or hands on the pads with a small bend in your elbows.
Bring the pads together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles.
Pause for a moment, then slowly open your arms back out until you feel a gentle stretch across your chest.
watchFor: Don't let your arms open further than a comfortable stretch. Going too far strains the front of your shoulders.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears, and don't use momentum to swing the pads together.

steps: Get on the floor on your hands and toes. Place your hands flat on the floor, a little wider than your shoulders, directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms one long, straight line from your head to your heels.
Tighten your stomach and squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag or rise up.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows angled back about 45 degrees from your body, not flared straight out.
Lower until your chest is a few inches from the floor, then push the floor away until your arms are straight.
watchFor: If you can't do a full push-up with a straight body yet, do them with your knees on the floor. It's the same movement with less weight.
Keep your neck in line with your spine. Look at a spot on the floor slightly ahead of your hands.
Keep your wrists flat and don't let your hips sag toward the floor.

steps: Find something sturdy and stable that won't move, like a bench or a strong box. Place your hands on the edge of it, a little wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body forms one straight line from head to heels, leaning at a slope.
Tighten your stomach and buttocks so your hips don't sag.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest to the edge of the surface, keeping your elbows angled back about 45 degrees from your body.
Push yourself back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Make sure the surface can't slide or tip. A wobbly surface can send you to the floor.
The higher the surface, the easier this is. Look for a lower surface as you get stronger.
Keep your body in one straight line and your wrists flat.

steps: Place your feet on a sturdy, stable surface like a bench, and put your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders, under your shoulders.
Your body should form one straight line from your head down to your heels, sloping downward toward your hands.
Tighten your stomach and squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, with your elbows angled back about 45 degrees from your body.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
watchFor: The higher your feet, the harder this is and the more weight rests on your shoulders. Start with a low surface.
Make sure the surface is stable and won't slide.
Don't let your lower back sag. Stop the set if you can't keep a straight line.

steps: Stand between two parallel bars (they're usually part of a dip station) and grab one in each hand. Jump or step up so your arms are straight and holding your whole body weight.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you. Lean your upper body forward a little, with your chest pointing toward the floor.
Slowly bend your elbows and lower your body, letting your elbows flare out slightly to the sides.
Lower until your upper arms are about level with the floor, or until you feel a comfortable stretch in your chest.
Push through your hands to lift yourself back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't go lower than level with the floor. Dropping further can strain your shoulders, and this is one of the moves most likely to cause shoulder pain.
Don't swing or bounce at the bottom.
If you can't lift your whole body weight yet, that's normal. Ask a gym staff member if there's a machine that takes some of your weight off, and build up gradually.

steps: Put on a weighted vest that fits snugly so it can't shift. If you don't have one, a training partner can rest a weight plate on your upper back once you're in position.
Get on the floor on your hands and toes, with your hands under your shoulders and a little wider than them.
Step your feet back so your body is one straight line from head to heels, and tighten your stomach and buttocks.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows angled back about 45 degrees from your body.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Only add weight once you can do this same movement with no extra weight and a perfectly straight body. Start with a very light load.
Make sure the weight can't slide off your back. A plate resting loosely on you is a hazard if you move suddenly.
Keep your wrists flat and your hips from sagging. Stop the set if your form breaks.

steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt, which is a belt with a chain that hangs a weight plate between your legs. Put the belt on around your waist. You can also hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the two parallel bars and lift yourself up so your arms are straight and you're holding your whole body weight plus the extra weight.
Lean your upper body forward slightly with your chest pointing toward the floor.
Slowly bend your elbows and lower yourself until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Push through your hands to lift yourself back up until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Only add weight once you can do this same movement with just your own body weight, smoothly and with good control. Start with a small weight.
Don't go lower than level with the floor. Deeper dips put a lot of stress on the shoulders, especially with extra weight.
Don't swing. Stay smooth and stop if your shoulders hurt.
